TARGET_CONCEPTS.label: Classical theism proof target
TARGET_CONCEPTS.description: The current proof target is not any vague ultimate. It is a personal, necessarily existing, omnipotent, omniscient, perfectly good creator or sustainer of reality.

attributes.omnipotence: maximal power, constrained by coherent possibility rather than contradictions
attributes.omniscience: complete knowledge of truths relevant to all reality
attributes.perfect_goodness: maximal moral perfection, directly exposed to evil and hiddenness constraints
attributes.necessary_existence: exists in every relevant possible world if it exists at all
attributes.creator_or_sustainer: ultimate ground, creator, or sustainer of contingent reality
attributes.relation_to_world: distinct from the world while grounding or sustaining it

TARGET_CONCEPTS.label: Deism comparator
TARGET_CONCEPTS.description: A creator or designer concept with weaker ongoing relational and revelatory commitments.

attributes.creator_or_sustainer: initial creator or designer, not necessarily ongoing sustainer
attributes.relation_to_world: often distant from ordinary religious experience and revelation

TARGET_CONCEPTS.label: Impersonal ultimate comparator
TARGET_CONCEPTS.description: An ultimate reality model that may be non-personal, nondual, or otherwise not classical theism.

attributes.necessary_existence: may be treated as ultimate or unconditional rather than personal necessity
attributes.relation_to_world: may be identity, nonduality, ground, or transcendence rather than creation

PREMISES.text: The target modal logic validates S5-style movement from possible necessity to necessity.
A maximally great or God-like being is metaphysically possible, not merely conceivable.
A strong principle of sufficient reason applies to contingent reality as a whole.
The universe or total contingent order requires an explanation outside itself.
Observed order or fine-tuning is better expected under intentional design than under live alternatives.
Objective moral facts exist and require a personal or divine ground.
Religious experiences and testimony carry evidential force after error models are discounted.
Decision theory can rationally recommend a religious commitment under uncertainty.

ARGUMENTS.name: Modal ontological argument
ARGUMENTS.thesis: If God-like necessary existence is possible in the right modal system, God exists necessarily.
ARGUMENTS.machine_status: validity can be proof-assistant checked; soundness depends on premises
blockers: possibility premise may beg the question
choice of modal logic is substantive
variants risk modal collapse or inconsistency

ARGUMENTS.name: Cosmological contingency argument
ARGUMENTS.thesis: Contingent reality requires a necessary ground, identified with God after attribute bridging.
ARGUMENTS.machine_status: partly formalizable; bridge from necessary ground to God remains open
blockers: strong PSR is denied by many alternatives
infinite regress and brute-fact options remain live
necessary ground does not yet entail personal, good, omniscient God

ARGUMENTS.name: Teleological and fine-tuning argument
ARGUMENTS.thesis: Order, purposiveness, or fine-tuning is evidence for intentional design.
ARGUMENTS.machine_status: probabilistic model can be implemented; priors and likelihoods dominate result
blockers: anthropic selection and multiverse hypotheses change likelihoods
biological design gaps are weakened by evolutionary explanation
probability measure over possible universes is unsettled

ARGUMENTS.name: Moral argument
ARGUMENTS.thesis: Objective moral normativity is best grounded in God.
ARGUMENTS.machine_status: requires a moral-realist ontology before formal proof search

ARGUMENTS.name: Religious experience and testimony
ARGUMENTS.thesis: Human religious experience is cumulative evidence for divine reality.
ARGUMENTS.machine_status: aggregatable as evidence, not a deductive proof
blockers: religious diversity underdetermines the target God concept
testimony is uneven and culturally mediated

ARGUMENTS.name: Pascal-style pragmatic argument
ARGUMENTS.thesis: Under some payoff matrices, theistic commitment can be rational even without proof.
ARGUMENTS.machine_status: can be implemented as expected-utility model; not an existence proof
blockers: many-gods objection changes the action space
belief may not be directly voluntary
rational commitment is not evidence of truth

WISDOM_CORPUS.summary: Godel/Scott-style ontological arguments can be represented and mechanically checked, but this checks validity under axioms rather than metaphysical soundness.
Ontological arguments face persistent challenges around existence, modality, conceivability, and whether the possibility premise assumes the conclusion.
Cosmological arguments move from contingency, causation, or sufficient reason to a necessary ground, then require a further bridge to God attributes.
Design and fine-tuning arguments can be modeled probabilistically, but the result depends on priors, alternatives, anthropic selection, and measure assumptions.
Cosmology supplies multiverse, anthropic-selection, and model-choice alternatives that must be evaluated before fine-tuning can support a God conclusion.
Moral arguments reason from morality or moral life toward God, while metaethical alternatives and divine-command objections remain live.
Religious experience can be evidence for subjects or communities, but cross-tradition diversity and error models limit direct proof strength.
Pascal-style arguments belong to rational commitment under uncertainty, not direct evidence that God exists.
Evil and divine hiddenness impose constraints on classical-theism proofs and must be handled before any final proof claim.
Cross-tradition models of ultimacy show that the proof target may be personal God, impersonal ultimate, nondual reality, or another ultimate category.
Religious experience must be classified across traditions because experience can support incompatible ultimacy models.
Naturalism provides ontological and methodological alternatives under which natural facts need not be explained by supernatural agency.
Atheism and agnosticism clarify the negation, suspension, and evidential standards that a proof of God must answer.
